intro: This API only reads data. The repo has no migrations, so a new local database stays empty. To see real data, the server needs a database that already holds the Treetracker data.
prerequisites: Node.js 20 and npm. CI tests on Node 20.
A `DATABASE_URL` for a database with the Treetracker data. The README asks you to join the Greenstand Slack channel for help with the database.

steps.title: Build the app
steps.text: This step compiles the TypeScript, as CI does.

steps.title: Run the tests
steps.text: These are the CI checks. The unit and repository tests need no database. At this commit, the integration tests do not run: `sh: 1: mocha: not found` (`mocha` is not in `package.json`). `npm test` still exits 0, because the repository tests run last.

steps.title: Set the connection URL
steps.text: Use the URL that you got from the team. You can also put it in a `.env` file (see `.env.example`). If you see `self signed certificate in certificate chain`, also set `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0`, as the README says.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.text: The API listens on http://localhost:3006 (for example, `/trees`). If the server cannot reach the database, it still starts, but each data request returns HTTP 500.
